Runs a short fixed CPU workload and a 64 MiB in-memory read/write workload. Results are informational, vary with device conditions, and should only be compared within the same app version.

Test left and right audio channels separately to verify stereo output.
Play a 1 kHz tone through the earpiece speaker. Hold the phone to your ear to listen.
Record audio and play it back to verify the microphone is working. Requires microphone permission.
Plug in wired headphones or a headset to test detection.
Press the hardware volume buttons to verify they are working.
Relative PCM amplitude only, not a calibrated sound-pressure or loudness measurement. Recorded audio stays in memory and is discarded when the test closes.
Confirm what you heard. Device detection alone cannot verify audible output.
Open front or rear camera, preview, and capture a photo to verify resolution.
Toggle the camera flash to verify the torch works.

Open each available test and follow its guidance. A pass requires a bounded sample or motion response.

Move the phone in different directions until a clear acceleration change is detected.
Rotate the phone until a clear angular movement is detected.
Change the phone orientation until the gravity vector changes.
Cover and uncover the proximity sensor near the top of the screen.
Move between brighter and darker light or cover the light sensor.
Turn the phone away from metal objects until the magnetic field changes.
Keep the phone still while five valid pressure samples are collected.
Walk at least one step while holding the phone.

Instantaneous current is shown as a positive magnitude. Direction follows the Android current sign unless battery status contradicts it; readings over 20 A are unavailable.
The OEM current sign contradicted battery status, so direction was normalized from the observed status.
This is Android’s current status value, not a battery capacity or wear diagnosis.
Samsung battery current reporting can vary by model and firmware.
Battery health details may be restricted by Samsung Knox.
Treat Samsung current as an instantaneous, low-confidence reading.
OnePlus current sign can vary during proprietary fast charging.
Battery status is used when the reported sign conflicts with the observed state.
Treat OnePlus current as an instantaneous, low-confidence reading.
Pixel current is read from the public Android battery API.
Treat Pixel current as an instantaneous, low-confidence reading.
This is Android’s current throttling status. Device-specific thermal design can affect how status and headroom correspond.
Live thermal status requires Android 10 or newer.
Android did not provide a current thermal status.
Live thermal monitoring could not be started.
A value of 1.0 is the device’s severe-throttling threshold. This unitless estimate is not a temperature and may be unavailable on supported Android versions.
Read from Android’s battery broadcast. This does not claim CPU, GPU, skin, or cooling-system temperature.
fonecheck does not create artificial thermal load. The snapshot describes only the device state observed while this screen or Full Check is active.

Writes and reads one 64 MiB temporary file in fonecheck’s private cache, then deletes it. You can cancel or skip the check.
Benchmark skipped. No temporary file was written.
Benchmark cancelled and temporary data cleanup requested.
Not run because the app cache does not have enough free space for the temporary file and safety reserve.
The storage benchmark could not be completed.
The temporary file did not read back with the expected size and checksum.
The benchmark completed, but Android could not confirm deletion of the temporary file.
Results reflect this app-cache run only. OS caching, thermal state, background activity, and device conditions can affect throughput.
What this check does not measure
Throughput is not physical flash health or wear. fonecheck does not inspect user files and does not apply a universal pass/fail speed threshold.

Review what fonecheck will do before any permission request appears.
You will inspect the display and use supported camera, motion, volume-button, vibration, speaker, and biometric checks.
Selected audio plays a short speaker tone and records a brief microphone sample for a relative level reading. Vibration can feel strong.
The storage benchmark writes, reads, and deletes one temporary 64 MiB file in fonecheck’s private cache.
Permissions are requested on the next screen only when needed. Denial limits coverage but does not fail or block the full check.
Unavailable hardware is marked not applicable. Every interactive check can be skipped or exited.
Report data stays on this device and is not uploaded. Raw audio, camera images, precise location, network names, and cell identifiers are not saved.
No internet or network-speed test is performed.
Allow the access you want to include, then continue. Missing or denied optional access is reported separately and never treated as hardware failure.
Reading device information and running bounded performance and app-private storage checks. The temporary 64 MiB storage file is deleted after the check.
Inspect each solid color for dead pixels, bright spots, shadows or burn-in.
Did every color look even and clean?
fonecheck plays a short speaker tone. Confirm whether you heard it clearly.
Each public camera opens a preview and captures one frame automatically.
Shake the phone gently. The test continues automatically when movement is detected.
fonecheck has just played a short vibration pattern. Patterned vibration can feel strong; stop, replay, confirm, or skip it at any time.
Press Volume Up and Volume Down once. fonecheck listens for the two key events for 15 seconds.
Use the biometric-only system prompt. A PIN, pattern, or password is not accepted as a biometric result.

fonecheck stores reports and preferences locally. It has no account, cloud sync, analytics, ads, or Internet permission.
fonecheck reports observations available through Android and user confirmations. It does not certify physical condition, safety, or repairability.

fonecheck includes open-source libraries. Their component inventory and applicable license terms are bundled below and in the release artifact.
Your onboarding choice could not be saved. Try again.
fonecheck brings device information, guided diagnostics, and saved reports into one clear place.
Safe checks can run automatically. Tests that need sight, sound, touch, movement, or another personal observation always ask you to confirm the result.
fonecheck does not upload diagnostic results. Data remains on this device unless you explicitly export or share a report.
Reports can contain technical device details. Review the destination before sharing an exported file.
Camera, microphone, location, phone, or nearby-device access is requested only when you start a check that needs it.
You can deny or skip a permission-dependent check. Opening Settings or this onboarding never requests a dangerous permission.
A saved report is an immutable record of that test session. Retesting creates a new snapshot, so comparisons never rewrite earlier evidence.
Run one diagnostic at a time or choose Full Check for a guided session. Results are diagnostic evidence, not a repair guarantee or certification.
Saved reports stay on this device until you delete them.

Touch-test grid. Drag across the whole area and place multiple fingers simultaneously.
Android reports that this device has no vibrator.
Long and patterned vibrations may feel strong or uncomfortable. Stop at any time.
If vibration is uncomfortable or cannot be perceived reliably, skip the physical confirmation. API capability remains reported separately.
API support means Android reports a native effect or primitive. It does not confirm that the vibration was physically felt.
Android apps cannot reliably test the power button, so it is not included in this test.
No failure is inferred. Try again or skip this test.
Device credential is shown as device context only. It is never accepted by this biometric test.
Not recognized. Try again in the system prompt or cancel it to exit this check.
A successful prompt confirms one enrolled biometric was accepted. It does not measure sensor quality or reveal enrolled templates.
Permission must be enabled in Settings
Microphone access is used only while you run the microphone diagnostic.
Camera access is used only for the camera preview, capture, and flash diagnostics.
Location access is required by Android to read nearby Wi-Fi and GPS diagnostic data.
Phone access is used to read SIM and mobile-network diagnostic data.
Nearby devices access is used to read Bluetooth diagnostic data on Android 12 and newer.
